correctness.rationale: For two states, compute the exact common affine slope q=e^{-(s+t)h} and the two Strang stationary intercepts p_A+u(p_B-p_A) and p_B+v(p_A-p_B). The strict sinh convexity bounds 0<u<t/(s+t), 0<v<s/(s+t) give a unique positive weight (unless generators commute) matching exact intercept; common slope then gives matrix equality. On the three-state path, A3^2=-2A3 and B3^2=-2B3 produce traces (1+z^2)(5+z^2)/4 versus 1+z+z^3, whose difference is (1-z)^4/4>0. The included independent-code verifier checks 300 binary numerical instances, 15 equal-rate examples and exact-rational trace polynomials.

value.rationale: An exactly stochasticity-preserving random selection of two split Markov subflows can reproduce the coupled binary transition operator at every h>0, including genuinely noncommuting equal-rate cases. A sharp minimal-dimension failure witness proves the mechanism is not a generic consequence of second-order splitting, providing an exact boundary relevant to Markov kinetic integrator design. No downstream cost guarantee or broad higher-dimensional impossibility is claimed.
